channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: Real-time visualization of G2L4 reverse transcriptase in DNA repair via microhomology-mediated end joining
item.description: The error-prone microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) pathway is important for double strand break repair. Here, the authors use high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize how the Pseudomonas aeruginosa chromosomally encoded group II intron-like reverse transcriptase (G2L4 RT) act on MMEJ substrates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetically engineered RNA inducers of proximity for protein regulation
item.description: Current genetic engineering techniques enable protein modulation at the DNA/RNA levels. Here, the authors design an RNA platform to bring target protein and effector enzyme into proximity, realizing direct protein regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Embryonic origin of cancer in newborn twins
item.description: Identical twins with the same cancer can reveal how childhood tumours arise and spread before birth. Here, the authors use whole-genome sequencing of tumour, normal and placental tissues to show that a sarcoma that originated in one twin spread to the other in utero , and trace early embryonic lineages that contributed differently to the twins and placenta.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk before and after a second booster in previously SARS-CoV-2 infected versus naïve COVAIL trial participants
item.description: Vaccines to SARS-CoV-2 clearly stimulate virus specific T cell and antibody responses but T cell-mediated protection is challenging to show. Here the authors use PBMC samples from an open-label clinical trial of different prototype and variant-specific COVID-19 vaccine boosters to examine the function and phenotype of T cell populations and how T cell response levels associate with risk of, and with protection against, symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: High potential contribution of intercropping to soybean and maize self-sufficiency in Europe
item.description: Domestic production of maize and soybeans in the EU currently falls short of demand. This study finds that adoption of maize-soybean intercropping could improve soybean self-sufficiency by 25−91% but also contribute to EU maize demand by 50−145%.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale metagenomic characterization of the vaginal microbiome and uropathogens in women with recent bacterial vaginosis and urinary tract infections
item.description: Here, the authors characterize shotgun vaginal metagenomic profiles from women across the US in relation to recent history of bacterial vaginosis and urinary tract infections, revealing the vagina as a reservoir for uropathogens.

item.title: Nature Communications: RhoA Y42C drives cell plasticity and PD-1-mediated immune evasion of diffuse gastric cancer
item.description: The oncogenic contribution of recurrent RHOA mutations in diffuse gastric cancer remains incompletely defined. Using engineered gastric organoids, the authors demonstrate that RHOA Y42C drives tumor formation and promotes PD-1- mediated immune suppression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Differential effects of visual and tactile deprivation on spatially modulated cells in the medial entorhinal cortex
item.description: How different types of sensory inputs modulate spatial representations is not fully understood. The authors show that rodents flexibly use visual and tactile cues in different contexts to maintain spatial maps, with distinct classes of spatially-modulated cells showing different sensitivities to sensory loss.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant pepinemab in combination with nivolumab and/or ipilimumab in resectable metastatic melanoma: a pilot biomarker-driven trial
item.description: Preclinical studies have suggested that blocking semaphorin 4D (SEMA4D) in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors can enhance anti-tumor immunity. Here the authors report the results of a pilot biomarker-driven neoadjuvant trial of the SEMA4D blocking antibody pepinemab in combination with nivolumab (anti-PD-1) and/or ipilimumab (anti CTLA-4) in patients with resectable metastatic melanoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gastrointestinal tract delivery of hydrogen by dynamic gas-releasing frameworks
item.description: Hydrogen therapy is limited by efficient storage and controlled release. Here, the authors show that gas-releasing frameworks enable high-capacity, sustained intestinal H 2 delivery for management of multiple inflammatory disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD
item.description: Here, the authors show that unstable airway microbial communities and their interactions with the immune system are linked to airway inflammation in people with HIV and COPD.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy: a phase II clinical randomized trial
item.description: The authors reported a randomized trial showing that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: The limits of Antarctic conservation governance
item.description: Many of Antarctica’s conservation threats originate beyond the region. This analysis of 90,000+ documents, finds that issues arising within Antarctica more clearly progress from discussion to governance action, while external threats often remain under deliberation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 ameliorates age-related intestinal hypomotility in older adults: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: Here, in a randomized, double-blind clinical trial in older adults, the authors show that probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 intervention reduces whole-gut transit time and remodels the gut microbiota suppressing bile salt hydrolase-expressing bacteria, further revealing a mechanistic role of taurochenodeoxycholic acid in the phenotype.

item.title: Nature Communications: High diversity but limited expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a peatland microbial community
item.description: Secondary metabolites, including metal chelators and antibiotics, are synthesized by diverse biosynthetic pathways. Here authors find that peatlands harbour extensive biosynthetic novelty, but their activation is only triggered by select conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis
item.description: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) can provide important benefits to childhood cancer patients, but clinical WGS workflows typically take weeks. Here, the authors evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of a rapid WGS research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics, reducing the mean turnaround time from 42 to 3 days without sacrificing the detection of clinically actionable variants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ghd7 ‑triggered transcriptional regulation for synergistically improving rice eating quality and yield
item.description: Rice breeders struggle to boost yield and eating quality simultaneously as the two traits often work against each other. Here, the authors identify a CCT domain transcription regulator encoding gene Ghd7 in determining rice grain amylose content and functioning in balancing starch and protein to coordinate yield and quality.

item.title: Nature Communications: TransGram for heterogeneity-aware transcriptome reconstruction from long read RNA-Seq data
item.description: Long-read RNA sequencing datasets exhibit heterogeneity that affects transcript reconstruction. Here, the authors characterize this heterogeneity and develop TransGram, which adapts reconstruction to different data types to improve accuracy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Characterization of silk-like materials from larval salivary glands of the dipteran, Keroplatus testaceus
item.description: Keroplatus testaceus uses a fibroin-free silk system composed of hydrophilic, collagen-like, and β-sheet proteins to produce two materials: a stretchable, adhesive mucus web for feeding and movement, and a stronger cocoon for pupal protection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stomatin organizes laterally segregated membrane microdomains to modulate transmembrane transport and signal transduction
item.description: Stomatin is thought to scaffold functional membrane microdomains; but how it works remains unclear. Here, authors reveal its 16-mer structure, identify cargo proteins, and show that the integrity of its cup-like complex is crucial for cell migration

item.title: Nature Communications: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
item.description: Decentralized diagnostics has the potential to improve health equity as well as support a more rapid response to disease outbreaks. Here authors present SID-WAVES, a multimodal microfluidic platform which allows ‘sample-in, results-out’ detection of both nucleic acid and protein biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of dasatinib in T follicular helper cell lymphomas
item.description: T follicular helper cell lymphomas (TFHL) depend on T cell receptor (TCR) signaling propagated by tyrosine kinases. Here, the authors conduct a phase 2 clinical trial of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib in TFHL, not meeting the prespecified primary endpoint (ORR = 23.5%), but correlating response with TCR signaling mutations.

item.title: Nature Communications: PSHIC reveals allele-specific chromatin organization by phasing-free structural modeling
item.description: PSHIC reconstructs parent-specific 3D genome organization from standard Hi-C data without phased genetic variants. It outperforms existing methods and recovers validated features of X inactivation, imprinting and gene regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fear learning–induced brain dynamics predict individual extinction memory expression following transcranial magnetic stimulation
item.description: Zhang et al. show that fear learning reshapes spontaneous brain activity and that these changes can predict individual differences in how extinction memories are later expressed following TMS-modulated extinction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ecological memory of prolonged plasmid persistence after transient antibiotic exposure
item.description: Zhou, Weiss and colleagues show that a brief antibiotic pulse can prolong plasmid persistence by removing plasmid-free competitors, creating an ecological memory that may sustain antimicrobial resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: RFWD3/FANCW orchestrates post-replicative filling of ssDNA gaps to promote UV tolerance
item.description: DNA lesions caused by UV light can block replication and generate single-stranded DNA gaps. Here, the authors reveal that the E3 ubiquitin ligase RFWD3 ubiquitylates RPA to prevent gap accumulation and promote DNA damage tolerance. This process helps maintain genome stability and regulates cell mutability.

item.title: Nature Communications: A randomized controlled trial of CDK7 inhibitor samuraciclib plus fulvestrant in advanced HR+/HER2− breast cancer
item.description: CDK7 is a therapeutic target in HR+/HER2- breast cancer due to its role in both cell cycle regulation and Estrogen Receptor transcription and activation. Here, the authors report a phase 2 randomised trial comparing samuraciclib (CDK7 inhibitor) plus fulvestrant (selective estrogen receptor degrader) against fulvestrant alone in patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer previously treated with CDK4/6 inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sexually dimorphic control of excitatory synapse maintenance in ventral hippocampal circuits by Neurexin2α ligand Vstm2b
item.description: This study identifies Vstm2b as a Neurexin2α ligand essential for sex- and input-specific maturation and maintenance of ventral hippocampal excitatory synapses. Loss of Vstm2b causes sexually dimorphic social deficits and increased anxiety in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transmembrane PhoxID: photoproximity labelling across the plasma membrane in vivo
item.description: Transmembrane proteins interact with molecules on both sides of the cell membrane to regulate cellular functions. Here, the authors develop tmPhoxID, a proximity labelling method that simultaneously maps proteins near both sides of transmembrane proteins in living mouse brains.

item.title: Nature Communications: Episodic changes in global forest edges in the 21st century
item.description: Forest edges are ecological frontiers that shape biodiversity and microclimate worldwide. The study maps their global change from 2000–2020 and reveals a 24 million-km decline, with contrasting regional trajectories and episodic shifts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fumarate hydratase deficiency triggers disulfidptosis under glucose deprivation
item.description: Cancer cells with defects in the metabolic enzyme fumarate hydratase (FH) are highly dependent on glucose and may be vulnerable to disruptions in redox balance. Here, the authors show that FH deficiency triggers disulfidptosis under glucose starvation through NADPH depletion and disulfide accumulation, and that complex I inhibition, including by metformin, can exploit this vulnerability to suppress FH-deficient tumor growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quasi-continuous cotranslational compaction and folding of a multidomain protein
item.description: Force Profile Analysis show that firefly luciferase folds co-translationally through a continuous compaction process, punctuated by a major subdomain folding event. Trigger Factor binds to the nascent chain at distinct steps in the folding profile.

item.title: Nature Communications: Electronically tuned N-terminal glycine selective bioconjugation enables in vitro and in vivo species-specific Staphylococcus aureus targeting
item.description: Methods for precisely targeting a biomolecule within living systems offer high potential for biomedical studies, but their development is limited by selectivity issues. Here, the authors introduce an electronically tunable chemical technology that targets N-terminal glycine and use the method for species-specific detection and inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus and its resistant strains, MRSA and VRSA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Aridity regulates scale-dependent effects of multiple resource additions on productivity stability in Eurasian grasslands
item.description: Increasing inputs of water and nutrients are reshaping grassland ecosystems worldwide, yet their ecological effects may vary across aridity gradients and spatial scales. The study shows that increasing aridity weakens the negative effects of multiple resource additions on large-scale productivity stability by reducing the stabilizing role of spatial asynchrony.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification and characterization of factors that govern apicoplast segregation in Toxoplasma gondii
item.description: Here, Mead et al. identify two apicoplast proteins, APP1 and APP2, in T. gondii, which are critical for anchoring the apicoplast to the centrosome and segregation machinery thereby facilitating its inheritance to the daughter cell during cell division.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benchmarking imputation methods on real-world clinical time series with simulated spatio-temporal missingness
item.description: This work proposes a model to simulate complex missingness structures in clinical data. When applying various imputation methods to fill gaps of missing data, simple linear models are more robust than complex deep learning techniques.

item.title: Nature Communications: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
item.description: Low throughput and extensive data processing in current proteomic workflows hinder rapid sample classification. Here, the authors introduce a deep-learning approach that directly accepts mass spectrometry-derived peptide ion profiles to rapidly classify cell states or patient disease status.

item.title: Nature Communications: A dedicated partitioning machinery ensures faithful inheritance of the apicoplast in Toxoplasma gondii
item.description: Many apicomplexan parasites possess an essential apicoplast organelle. Here, Eichlin et al. identify APP proteins in T. gondii , which are critical for anchoring the apicoplast to the centrosome and the cytoskeleton, thereby facilitating its inheritance during cell division.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale proteomics identifies circulating markers of pulmonary pressure and pulmonary hypertension risk
item.description: By integrating proteomics, genetics and imaging, this study identifies candidate blood biomarkers of pulmonary hypertension, implicates NOTCH3 in disease development, and defines distinct biological subtypes of individuals at risk for this condition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantifying parks as preventive health assets using population-scale mobility data
item.description: Using mobile-phone data from Greater Tokyo, the authors find that parks generate measurable walking-related health benefits, but returns vary widely. Smaller neighborhood parks often offer stronger investment potential than large destination parks.

item.title: Nature Communications: A family of small proteins links c-di-GMP riboswitch signaling with sporulation in Clostridioides difficile
item.description: The second messenger c-di-GMP inhibits sporulation in the pathogenic bacterium Clostridioides difficile through unclear mechanisms. Here, Badilla Lobo et al. show that the expression of sporulation genes is modulated by a family of small membrane-associated proteins encoded by genes that are controlled by c-diGMP-regulated riboswitches.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
item.description: A multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform was established by conjugating NA inhibitors and Fc domain. AVCs cross-link flu viruses, blocking entry and release. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate outperformed clinical drugs in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
item.description: Feasibility and safety profile of intratumoral administration of a DC vaccine overexpressing CCL21 (CCL21-DC) have been previously reported in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here the authors report safety, clinical outcomes and immunological correlates of a phase I trial of CCL21-DC in combination with anti-PD1 pembrolizumab in patients with advanced NSCLC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Herbicide degradation is driven by communication-mediated division of labor in synthetic communities
item.description: Herbicide residues threaten soil health. Researchers constructed two SynComs that degrade multiple herbicides via quorum sensing-mediated metabolic division of labor, and maize pot trials verify their bioremediation efficacy.

item.title: Nature Communications: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
item.description: Slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels is important for regulating cellular excitability. Here the authors probe the conformational dynamics in the selectivity filter using smFRET and reveal the critical residue pair that mediates conformational communication between the primary and slow inactivation gates

item.title: Nature Communications: Top-down semantic predictions align phonetic neuronal dynamics in human superior temporal gyrus
item.description: How semantic information influences phonetic processing during speech perception remains unclear. Here, the authors show that semantic predictions reshape phonetic representations in human temporal cortex at the level of neuronal population activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: DCAF7 regulates hematopoietic stem cell function and differentiation through polycomb repressive complex 1 modulation
item.description: This study identifies DCAF7 as a new regulator of blood stem cells showing how it controls chromatin to preserve stem cell function with implications for understanding normal and malignant blood formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Saturation mutagenesis enables RAD51D clinical variant interpretation and identifies distinct biochemical functions
item.description: RAD51D is a tumor suppressor gene where pathogenic variants are associated with increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer. This study reports a high throughput functional screen of 6,888 RAD51D coding variants along with analysis of 70 clinically-identified breast and ovarian cancer variants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
item.description: Russell et al. introduce a 10 × faster, chemically detailed chromatin model bridging molecular and genomic scales, revealing how DNA sequence, spacing and histone acetylation govern chromatin folding and phase separation.

Nature Communications: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model using FDG-PET imaging to accurately predict Alzheimer’s-type tau pathology across spectrums of aging and dementia, providing a novel framework to estimate tau burden non-invasively.

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
item.description: In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
item.description: Early risk prediction is essential to decide the treatment procedure for pediatric acute myeloid leukemia. Here, the authors show that rare chemoresistant cell populations, detectable at diagnosis, improve risk stratification and reveal potential targets for more effective, personalized therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune correlates of protection are exposure-dependent: evidence from the Dominican Republic
item.description: This study shows that antibody levels linked to protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection vary with transmission intensity, suggesting immune correlates of protection depend on exposure context.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
item.description: Subchondral bone remodeling is increasingly implicated in osteoarthritis, but its spatial organization remain incompletely understood. This study provides a high-resolution spatial map of subchondral bone and identifies conserved spatial architectures, revealing distinct microenvironmental states and candidate signaling pathways associated with subchondral bone sclerosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cannabinoid modulation of central amygdala population dynamics during threat investigation
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying cannabinoids’ anxiogenic effects are not fully understood. Here authors show that cannabinoids dose-dependently increased spontaneous activity of central amygdala (CeA) neurons expressing somatostatin (SOM), altered CeA activity patterns during threat processing, and enhanced defensive behavior. Ex vivo studies in brain slices further showed that cannabinoids reduce inhibitory input from neighboring neurons, releasing a “brake” on SOM activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ -driven uveal melanomas
item.description: Uveal melanoma (UM) is often driven by mutations in GNAQ. Here, authors identify p300 as a synthetic lethal target in GNAQ-mutant UM and show that p300 inhibition impairs tumour growth and metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tonicity drives collecting duct maturation in the mammalian kidney
item.description: Organ maturation is an emerging focus in the fields of organoid and developmental biology. The authors show that high tonicity drives the maturation of renal collecting ducts in vitro and in vivo, improving morphology, gene expression, and function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial
item.description: Here the authors report the results of a multicenter, double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that evaluates the effect and safety of different concentration atropine eyedrops (0.01%, 0.04%, 0.10%) for myopia control in children with high myopia. The findings show that nightly use of 0.10% atropine eye drops for 24 months mitigated myopia progression with an acceptable safety profile.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
item.description: Here, Pulliam and colleagues characterize the metabolites encoded by tumor-inhabiting microbes and their potential role in cancer pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K + channel
item.description: The process by which the voltage sensor electromechanically couples to the pore in K+ channels is not fully understood. A cryo-EM structure of a partially activated state, together with computational modeling and MD simulations, clarifies the mechanistic basis for electromechanical coupling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Untargeted screening of drug-like compounds using high-throughput metabolomics uncovers inhibitors of key biological pathways
item.description: Metabolomics is widely used in drug development to reveal mechanisms of action. Here, the authors identify drug-like compounds with potent enzyme engagement by screening 1,020 compounds of unknown function, allowing them to discover nucleotide synthesis inhibitors and an atrophy reversing glutathione activator.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization
item.description: Protein structures are increasingly available but turning them into useful drug candidates remains difficult. Here, Cao et al. introduce MolGenBench to assess 17 generative methods and reveal gaps in activity, target awareness and generalization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Substrate coupling and inhibition in human Na + -dependent Cl − /HCO 3 − exchanger NCBE (SLC4A10)
item.description: NCBE (SLC4A10) is important for cerebrospinal fluid pH regulation. Here, authors determine cryo-EM structures of human NCBE that reveal ion binding, inhibitor recognition, and the structural basis of substrate coupling in this transporter.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation tunes electrostatically driven protein-RNA interactions
item.description: Phosphorylation can alter the charge of intrinsically disordered proteins and thereby regulate their interactions. Here, the authors show that phosphorylation acts as an electrostatic rheostat for SRSF1- RNA binding, with binding free energy varying approximately linearly with net charge.

item.title: Nature Communications: PrimPol toggled by ATR modulates fork slowing and repriming under oncogenic KRAS-induced replication stress
item.description: Oncogenic KRAS causes replication stress that threatens genome stability during cancer development. Here, the authors show that ATR-regulated PrimPol switches between fork slowing and repriming modes to help cells tolerate KRAS-induced replication stress while limiting error-prone DNA synthesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
item.description: Reverting waste carbon into chemicals with minimal freshwater use is essential for a sustainable future. Here, the authors engineer the marine bacterium R. nubinhibens , by decoupling bioproduction from central metabolism to convert lignin into chemicals with seawater as a water source.

item.title: Nature Communications: Amygdala beta bursts modulate hippocampal neuronal dynamics during human emotional processing
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying emotional processing are not fully understood. Using intracranial recordings in humans, this study finds that transient amygdala beta bursts are associated with valence-dependent hippocampal neuronal activity, revealing temporally precise dynamics of emotional processing.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers
item.description: Plant sensors are emerging as key tools for precision agriculture, yet continuous monitoring of biomarkers in plant biofluids remains underdeveloped. Here, the authors introduce PlantIonics, a wearable microfluidic electrochemical platform for multiplexed, in situ analysis of guttation fluid. The system enables continuous, noninvasive monitoring of stress-associated plant physiological and metabolic responses under changing environmental conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping
item.description: Optical genome mapping (OGM) provides long-range genomic information but relies on sparse enzymatic labeling that restricts resolution in poorly labeled or structurally complex regions. Here the authors assemble yeast genomes at chromosome scale using dense OGM, resolving large repetitive regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa
item.description: In this study, the authors show that post-treatment desethylamodiaquine concentration is the primary pharmacokinetic determinant of protection against malaria infection in African children who are given sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, with little apparent effect from sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.

Nature Communications: Metabolization of human milk oligosaccharides by Streptococcus pneumoniae
item.description: It is unclear whether human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) can be used as a nutrient source by Streptococcus pneumoniae . Here, Bacher et al. report that these bacteria can metabolize several HMOs, identify genes and pathways involved in the process, and show that a non-metabolizable HMO inhibits pneumococcal adherence to host cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Repurposing Cas12a2-mediated abortive infection for efficient and low-toxicity microbial genome editing
item.description: Microbial genome engineering is often limited by toxicity from existing selection methods. Here, the authors develop a Cas12a2-based RNA-guided editing strategy that improves efficiency and reduces cellular damage, providing a robust tool for microbial engineering.

item.title: Nature Communications: WeedNet: a foundation model-based global-to-local AI approach for weed species identification and classification
item.description: Weeds consistently threaten crop yields worldwide, making early and accurate identification essential for effective management. Trained on 14 million images representing 1,593 weed species, WeedNet achieved 91% global accuracy and, through global-to-local fine-tuning, reached 97% accuracy for Iowa weeds.

item.title: Nature Communications: 3D Reconstruction of Dinoflagellate Chromosomes from Hi-C Data Challenges the Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Hypothesis
item.description: Philipp et al. model 3D chromosome conformations from Hi-C and RNA-seq data from three dinoflagellate species, challenging long-held assumptions about cholesteric liquid crystal organization and transcriptional enrichment at chromosome peripheries.

item.title: Nature Communications: PIP5K-Ras bistability triggers plasma membrane symmetry breaking to define cellular polarity and regulate migration
item.description: As cells polarize and migrate, numerous molecular events critical for immunity and cancer metastasis dynamically self-organize. This study identifies a universal symmetry-breaking mechanism where locally active Ras GTPase and lipid kinase PIP5K complete a mutually inhibitory circuit.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cep57 organizes pericentriolar material through dual architectural modules and prevents human mosaic variegated aneuploidy
item.description: Cep57 bridges centriolar microtubules and the pericentriolar material to organize centriole biogenesis. Structural, biochemical, and patient cell analyses reveal how disruption of this architecture causes centrosome defects underlying MVA2 syndrome.

item.title: Nature Communications: RuPHOTACs provide photocontrol over protein degradation with optimized properties for biological applications
item.description: PROTACs offer a powerful strategy to eliminate disease-relevant proteins, but off-target activity in healthy tissues remains a major challenge. Here, the authors introduce Ruthenium-based PHOToActivated Chimeras (RuPHOTACs), a new class of light-responsive PROTACs that remain inactive until triggered by low-energy light.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clock neurons modulate seizure timing through a diurnal switch
item.description: Neural mechanisms that drive diurnal oscillations in seizure susceptibility are not fully understood. Here, in this manuscript, fruit flies show the daily rhythm of seizure risks, driven by brain clock neurons and independent of sleep amount. Silencing these neurons suppressed seizures, further demonstrating the role for brain clock neurons in modulating daily seizure risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sphingolipids associate with the chlamydial nucleoid and mark developmental transitions in Chlamydia trachomatis
item.description: During the developmental cycle of the pathogenic bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis , non-replicative bacterial cells (elementary bodies, EBs) alternate with replicative forms within membrane-bound inclusions within infected host cells. Here, the authors identify sphingolipid derivatives within the highly condensed DNA nucleoids of EBs, suggesting a potential role for this lipid in stage-specific DNA condensation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cell-autonomous restoration of splicing homeostasis and RP11 phenotype in patient-derived RPE and retinal organoids by PRPF31 .AAV gene therapy
item.description: PRPF31 gene therapy restores RNA splicing and reverses cellular dysfunction in patient-derived retinal models of retinitis pigmentosa. The treatment cures advanced cellular defects, highlighting a wide window for clinical intervention.

item.title: Nature Communications: IAP antagonist tolinapant (ASTX660) in combination with pembrolizumab in advanced solid tumors: a phase I trial
item.description: The IAP antagonist ASTX660 has the potential to enhance cancer immunotherapy by sensitizing tumour cells to immune-mediated killing. Here, the authors report results from an open-label, multicentre phase I trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of ASTX660 in combination with the anti-PD-1 antibody pembrolizumab.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multilayer MEG source modelling enables depth-resolved laminar inference in humans
item.description: Researchers developed a multilayer MEG framework that estimates activity across cortical depth non-invasively. Simulations and three human datasets show when reliable laminar inference is possible, enabling studies of cortical microcircuit dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Programmable DNA protonuclei reveal environmental context on protein phase separation
item.description: Protein phase separation is often investigated in dilute solution, meaning that the influence of the crowded environmental context of cells is often overlooked. Here, the authors introduce a programmable DNA-based platform to probe the phase behavior of proteins within a more biomimetic environment.

item.title: Nature Communications: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
item.description: In this exploratory randomized trial, the monoclonal antibody AER002 was safe but did not improve clinical or biomarker outcomes in Long COVID. Post-hoc findings suggest baseline antibody levels and drug exposure may inform future studies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification of functional bacterial-viral pneumotypes associated with airway inflammation and all-cause mortality in critically ill patients
item.description: Here, the authors identify high-risk viral-bacterial functional pneumotypes associated with all-cause mortality in critically ill patients, which are characterized by expansion of virulent bacteriophages, depletion of health-associated bacteria, and lung inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A role for selective ER autophagy in gametogenic rejuvenation revealed by high-throughput lifespan profiling
item.description: Gametogenesis fully resets lifespan, although how this is achieved is unclear. Here, Spiri et al. developed a high-throughput assay to study this rejuvenation event in yeast, revealing selective autophagy of the ER as a key molecular mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multifunctional PKS-NRPS megasynthetase in nematodes produces divergent signaling molecules that control different developmental arrests
item.description: A polyketide synthase (PKS)-nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) hybrid assembly line that is expressed in the canal-associated neurons of Caenorhabditis elegans promotes recovery from starvation-induced larval arrest. Here, the authors show that in the predatory nematode Pristionchus pacificus , this PKS-NRPS assembly line produces diverse secondary metabolites, which regulate starvation-induced larval arrest and development of the dauer larval stage.

item.title: Nature Communications: Religious celibacy is linked to marriage and wealth transmission practices across different world religions
item.description: Lifelong religious celibacy has been linked to sibling competition over parental wealth. Here, the authors show that celibacy is linked to marriage patterns, and its prevalence among men and women is related to which sex faces higher marriage payments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural mechanisms underlying resistance to Switch-II pocket inhibitors in KRAS
item.description: This study explores how clinically observed KRAS resistance mutations alter drug-binding interactions and dynamics of the Switch-II pocket while preserving oncogenic signaling, providing a structural framework for developing more durable KRAS inhibitors.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep-learning single-cell profiling uncovers interbacterial and drug-driven reshaping of pathogen virulence
item.description: This study introduces MALVINA, a deep-learning platform that measures bacterial invasion and DNA damage in individual human cells, revealing how bacterial interactions and commonly used drugs reshape pathogen virulence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion
item.description: By depleting cohesin, the authors show that changes in 3D enhancer-promoter contacts alter enhancer regulatory effects. But only a subset of enhancer-promoter pairs shows weakened 3D contacts, explaining why only some genes change in expression.

item.title: Nature Communications: A SAGA-like AP2-P-ARP1-GCN5 transcriptional complex targets pathogenesis-associated genes during the blood-stage development of Babesia gibsoni
item.description: This study characterizes a novel SAGA-like epigenetic regulatory module in Babesia gibsoni, composed of the ApiAP2 transcription factor AP2-P, ARP1 and histone acetyltransferase GCN5. This complex modulates chromatin accessibility and binds specific genomic motifs to control the expression of genes involved in parasite invasion, antigenic variation, drug resistance and stage conversion, critically supporting parasite blood-stage growth and pathogenicity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Zona incerta somatostatin + neurons modulate seizure progression through hypothalamic circuits
item.description: The role of zona incerta (ZI) GABAergic subtypes in regulating epileptic seizures remains elusive. The authors find that ZI somatostatin + GABAergic neurons bidirectionally control seizure spread via projections onto ventromedial hypothalamus, serving as a potential therapeutic target for epilepsy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chlorophyll as a sustainable crosslinking strategy for engineering highly compressible hydrogels
item.description: Hydrogels with high deformation and resilience are desirable for applications such as injectable cardiac patches. Here, authors provide a strategy using chlorophyll as a physical crosslinker to engineer highly compressible hydrogels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Independent assembly of the flight apparatus in a non-avian dinosaur clade
item.description: Microraptorines were bird-like dinosaurs that possessed some flight adaptations. A new fossil species from the early Cretaceous, Norellraptor barsboldi , suggests that this group evolved their own flight ability independently from the main lineage of modern birds.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-molecule imaging reveals DNA shape read-out by the INO80 chromatin remodeler
item.description: How chromatin remodelers regulate nucleosome positioning remains poorly understood. Here, the authors use single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to reveal how read-out of DNA shape features regulates INO80 DNA interactions and remodeling activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pulsed electromagnetic fields activate a peripheral interoceptive pathway to suppress sympathetic Npy for osteogenesis
item.description: Here, the authors show that neuropeptide Y drives stress-induced osteoporosis by promoting bone marrow adipocyte senescence and impairing bone formation. Pulsed electromagnetic field treatment reverses this via sensory nerve-derived SEMA3A, which suppresses neuropeptide Y through a local circuit.

item.title: Nature Communications: Limosilactobacillus reuteri for oral mucositis in patients undergoing radiotherapy for malignant head and neck tumors: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: Oral mucositis is an important complication for patients with head and neck cancer undergoing radiotherapy. Here the authors report the results of a randomized phase II comparing the activity of the probiotic Limosilactobacillus reuteri vs placebo in alleviating oral mucositis in patients with head and neck cancer receiving radiotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Membrane damage induces TagQ/TagR complex-mediated H1-T6SS assembly in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
item.description: The H1-T6SS of Pseudomonas aeruginosa assembles in response to membrane damage. Here, the authors show that this response mechanism is regulated by the formation of a complex between the membrane lipoprotein TagQ and the periplasmic protein TagR.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial control of karyopherin binding avidity within NPC mimics revealed by designer FG-nucleoporins
item.description: By designing artificial FG-Nucleoporins (Nups), the authors investigate how the FG-Nup amino acid sequence controls transport selectivity in nuclear pores, with the avidity between FG-Nups and transport receptors playing a key role.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reaction enhancement via product scavenging and phase separation-driven pathway canalization
item.description: Catalysts can be slowed when reaction products remain bound to them. Here, authors design scavengers that remove these products and use droplet-like compartments to keep the scavengers away from unreacted reactants, accelerating nucleic acid enzyme reactions by approximately 230-fold.

item.title: Nature Communications: mHolmes improves cross anatomical cadaveric microbiome forecasting for postmortem interval estimation
item.description: This study presents mHolmes, a transfer-learning framework that forecasts postmortem microbiome changes across body sites, improving postmortem interval estimation and highlighting microbial features with forensic potential.

item.title: Nature Communications: The plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 forms oligomeric complexes and senses broader proteolytic activity
item.description: Using electron microscopy, the authors describe the conformational changes induced when the plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 is cleaved and activated. Moreover, oligomerization of cleaved ITIH4 is shown not to impact protease inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli
item.description: Tungsten-dependent enzyme production is limited by complex metal cofactor requirements and poor compatibility with expression hosts. Here the authors engineer E. coli to support the aerobic production of various tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases.

item.title: Nature Communications: “Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition”
item.description: The neural control of LUT (lower urinary tract) function is not fully understood. Here authors demonstrate that transcriptionally distinct enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus are recruited during voiding to selectively control external urethral sphincter relaxation and regulate urinary behaviors in a sex-specific manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Response-Adapted Postoperative Therapy Following Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: a phase II trial
item.description: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy has emerged as a promising approach for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), but its implications for postoperative treatment remain uncertain. This phase 2 study reports efficacy outcomes of response-adapted postoperative therapy following sintilimab plus paclitaxel and cisplatin in patients with resectable HNSCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diminished sialoside binding in novel H5N1 influenza hemagglutinin variants identified in a human patient
item.description: This study explores the biochemical and structural roles of hemagglutinin mutations identified in a human case of H5N1 influenza and reports effects of the mutations in patient viral populations on sugar binding and membrane fusion.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global spatiotemporal dynamics of mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections over the past three decades
item.description: Long-term mortality from carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections is poorly characterised worldwide. Here, authors analyse data from 204 countries and territories, revealing divergent trajectories by region, pathogen, and pandemic period.

item.title: Nature Communications: Age-dependent alterations in human striatum identify a PPP1R15B-miR-196a node as a modifier of Huntington’s disease
item.description: Researchers show that age-dependent upregulation of the proteostasis regulator R15B contributes to Huntington’s disease pathology. Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of R15B cleared mutant protein aggregates and reversed neurodegeneration in HD models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early insights into predicted efficacy of Ebola monoclonal antibodies for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
item.description: Rapid predictive methods narrow the solution space in an outbreak setting. In this computational study, the authors find that cocktail treatments for Ebola Zaire could be more effective than monotherapies against the 2026 Bundibugyo strain.

item.title: Nature Communications: SpaCEy links spatial tissue patterns to clinical outcomes using explainable graph neural networks
item.description: SpaCEy uses explainable graph neural networks to link spatial tissue organisation with clinical outcomes, identifying spatial and molecular patterns associated with cancer progression and patient survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct inflammatory marker profiles of adolescents and young adults among the HIV risk, infection, and treatment spectrum
item.description: Nielsen-Saines and colleagues identify unique and divergent immune perturbations across groups of youth living with or at risk of HIV. Their findings shed light on conserved and stage-specific that may underlie variations in outcomes and treatment success for HIV.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial multi-omics reveals disease-associated oligodendrocytes and metabolic dysregulation in male Parkinson’s disease mouse models
item.description: Spatial multi-omics of Parkinson’s disease mouse models identifies a disease-associated oligodendrocyte state in which IL-33 signalling to microglial ST2 shapes alpha-synuclein clearance, alongside regional lipid and glutamate metabolic disruption.

item.title: Nature Communications: An epigenetic aging-informed dietary pattern is associated with a spectrum of aging-related health outcomes
item.description: Diet is associated with biological aging, but few dietary indices have been designed to specifically target epigenetic aging. Here, the authors develop EDISEA, a food-based dietary index predictive of slower GrimAge2 aging, and show that higher scores are associated with slower epigenetic aging, lower mortality, and reduced risks of age-related diseases

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice
item.description: Chronic stress can promote hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. Here, the authors show in mice that chronic stress activates a brain-liver signaling circuit that mediates tumor epithelial-macrophage crosstalk and promotes HCC growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extended dosing intervals enhance the durability of a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against pandemic H5N1 influenza: a randomized, observer-blind, dose-finding Phase I study
item.description: Here, the authors present a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial of ARCT-2304, a bicistronic self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against H5N1 influenza. The findings support a potential role for self-amplifying mRNA platforms against influenza.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reoviridae -derived short trimerization domain for stabilizing homo-trimerization of vaccine immunogens and therapeutic proteins
item.description: In this study, the authors engineer a short trimerization tag for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. The tag enables a trimeric ACE2 decoy that exhibits broad neutralizing activity against coronaviruses and confers protection in animal models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal characterization of Alzheimer disease pathology in living human brain tissue
item.description: This study uses brain biopsies collected during shunt surgery to examine early Alzheimer disease in living brain tissue, showing rapid tau turnover and stable amyloid plaques.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy interferes with tertiary lymphoid structure formation in Epstein-Barr virus-associated gastric cancer
item.description: Efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with EBV-associated gastric cancer (EBVaGC) remains controversial. Here the authors show that, by promoting EBV reactivation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, NAC disrupts tertiary lymphoid structure formation in patients with EBVaGC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systemic and Mucosal Antibody Responses Against Neisseria gonorrhoeae ( Ng ) Outer Membrane Vesicle Antigens following Four-Component Meningococcal Serogroup B (4CMenB) Immunization in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Phase II Trial
item.description: This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial shows that a two-dose series of 4CMenB vaccine induces both systemic and mucosal IgG responses to Neisseria gonorrhoeae, suggesting a potential role in gonorrhea prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Elevated ozone activates maternal immunity to drive offspring IgG-mediated anaphylaxis through IgG glycosylation alterations
item.description: Environmental pollution may have effects upon unborn children. Here the authors look at human retrospective data and use mouse models to show that ozone exposure during pregnancy can promote allergy susceptibility in adult offspring and this may involve changes in IgG glycosylation and increased inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gα12/13 deficiency attenuates obesity-associated adipose tissue inflammation and promotes energy expenditure
item.description: Obesity impairs adipose function and drives metabolic disease. Here, the authors show that obesity-induced Gα12/13 restrains β-adrenergic signaling; its loss raises energy expenditure and protects mice from diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized single-cell transcriptomics reveals molecular diversity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Personalized functional genomics atlas for Alzheimer’s disease that uses knowledge-guided graph neural networks to analyze donor-level functional genomics, identify disease subpopulations and trajectories, and link genetic variants to gene regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-pathogen pyrimidine metabolism drives cystic fibrosis lung disease
item.description: Here, Lohia et al show that pyrimidine metabolism is a driver of pulmonary remodelling and bacterial infection in people with cystic fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages
item.description: Induction of trained immunity can elicit anti-tumor effects. Here the authors show that histone deacetylase inhibitor preconditioning elicits a IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in monocytes/macrophages, promoting anti-tumor immunity in multiple triple negative breast cancer models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Risk stratification for MDR/RR-TB: a comprehensive integrated patient-level analysis from TB programs and contemporary clinical trials
item.description: Pooling data from 7750 patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis worldwide, in this study, the authors defined disease-severity phenotypes based on clinical and treatment features, stratifying patients by risk of unfavourable outcomes to enable risk-adapted, stratified care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Attractin-like protein 1 is an essential partner of MC4R to regulate body weight
item.description: The authors identified ATRNL1 as a key regulator of MC4R for appetite control. Loss of ATRNL1 or damaging ATRNL1 variants result in impaired MC4R signaling, increased food intake and promote weight gain. Mutations in Atrnl1 could contribute to obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of laminin mimicry by E. coli CNF1 and its therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy
item.description: The authors show how the bacterial toxin CNF1 mimics laminin to hijack its cell-surface receptor BCAM, and how this interaction can be repurposed to guide T cells to selectively kill BCAM-expressing cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Long-range interdependencies aware signal analysis for rapid and accurate obstructive sleep apnea prediction
item.description: Researchers develop a framework that captures long-range physiological interactions from sleep recordings to predict obstructive sleep apnea severity. Validated in more than 35,000 individuals, it shows robust performance across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mortality and healthcare services in Pennsylvania state prisons following extreme ambient temperatures
item.description: Extreme hot and cold temperatures are determinants of mortality for incarcerated populations and this manuscript shows that temperature extremes increase demand on already strained prison healthcare systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Five-country analysis of geographic and dietary drivers of gut microbiome composition and genomic variation
item.description: In this study, authors show that human gut microbiome composition and microbial genomes vary strongly across five industrialized countries, with diet microbiome links that are partly shared but largely population-specific.

item.title: Nature Communications: RIPK3 acts as a molecular switch between neuroprotection and neuropathology during herpes simplex encephalitis
item.description: HSV-1 encephalitis causes severe brain injury, but the mechanism of immune pathology remains to be explored. The authors here show that RIPK3 drives astrocyte death though benefits viral control in other cell types, further RIPK3 inhibition promotes survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combinatorial targeting of the miR-379/miR-410 cluster normalizes glucose and lipid homeostasis in male models of diabetes and obesity
item.description: Hepatic-specific repression of the miR-379/miR-410 cluster in adult mice impacts hepatic insulin signalling and affects whole-body glucose and lipid metabolism, improving glycemic control and dyslipidemia in male models of obesity and diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Anti-thymocyte globulin triggers TNF-dependent cell death in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
item.description: Anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) is a potent immunosuppressant used to prevent and treat acute organ transplant rejection and severe aplastic anemia. Here, the authors discover that ATG can be repurposed to induce TNF-driven cell death in T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bayesian bilevel operator learning with low-rank adaptation for efficient uncertainty quantification of PDE inverse problems
item.description: Estimating parameters of partial differential equations from data with quantified uncertainty is computationally demanding. Here, authors combine bilevel local operator learning with low rank adaptation to enable efficient gradient-based posterior sampling without adjoint equations, pretraining data, or sampling network weights.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ociperlimab and tislelizumab in advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (AdvanTIG-203): a phase II study
item.description: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors improving survival outcomes in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) but the survival rates of some subsets ESCC population are still poor. Here this group reports a phase 2 randomized trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of ociperlimab and tislelizumab in patients with PD-L1 TAP ≥ 10%, unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide cross-trait analysis to compare genetic architecture between Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits
item.description: Parkinson’s disease has been epidemiologically linked to kidney function, but the extent of their shared genetic basis remains unclear. Here, the authors integrate genome-wide genetic correlation, pleiotropy and colocalisation analyses to identify shared loci and candidate pathways connecting Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases
item.description: Here, the authors develop injectable arterial organoids that form functional vascular networks in vivo, promoting blood flow restoration and tissue repair in models of ischemic disease by enhancing vascular regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct migratory dendritic cell subsets cooperate to prime tissue-resident memory-like CD8⁺ T cells in mouse tumors
item.description: Tissue-resident memory (T RM ) CD8 + T cells in the tumor microenvironment are relevant for anti-tumor immunity and immune checkpoint blockade response. Here, the authors conditionally ablate type 1 and type 2 dendritic cells in a lung cancer mouse model, finding both to be critical for the differentiation and expansion of T RM -like T cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Omaveloxolone functions as a molecular crowbar-like degrader of STING to alleviate aging-related inflammation
item.description: Aging-related inflammation can have excessive activation of the STING pathway as some of its features. Here the authors look at the function of Omaveloxolone and show this compound binds to the base of the STING ligand-binding domain and destabilises STING leading to STING K27-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and show Omaveloxolone reducing aging associated inflammation in aged male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nano-NucleOTAC-mediated Z-DNA transformation disrupts mycobacterium tuberculosis biofilms and activates antibacterial immunity
item.description: Extracellular DNA (eDNA) from tuberculosis can protect bacteria from host immune responses and antibiotics and can contain Z form eDNA which is harder for DNase to hydrolyze. Here the authors use a nanoparticle system to more specifically target eDNA and the Z form and show cleavage of Z-DNA and improvement of immune responses against TB infection in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proximity biotinylation at the host- Shigella interface reveals UFMylation as an antibacterial pathway
item.description: Here, López-Jiménez et al. develop a proximity biotinylation approach to map the host-bacterial interface and show that intracellular Shigella and Salmonella are targeted by UFMylation, a ubiquitin-like system.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ambient, real-time digitization and datafication of glass slide microscopy towards AI-at-the-microscope
item.description: HistoCAM ambiently captures the pathologist’s full, optically sampled microscope view, enabling real-time digital and AI tools while turning routine slide review into process-aware, AI-ready data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Development-inspired approach for the derivation of functional and transplantable salivary gland organoids from human pluripotent stem cells
item.description: Here, they generate salivary gland epithelial progenitors hPSCs by mimicking in vivo salivary gland development. These progenitors self-assemble into salivary gland organoids in vitro and reconstituted both acinar and ductal structures upon orthotopic transplantation in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transient activation of ciliary CCR2 signaling promotes the initiation of adipogenesis
item.description: Obesity is linked to chronic inflammation and enhanced adipogenesis. Here, the authors show that preadipocytes transiently form CCR2-enriched primary cilia, allowing inflammatory CCL2 to activate ciliary CCR2 and drive ERK-dependent adipogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiopulmonary hospitalization risks from wildfire-specific and non-wildfire PM 2.5 in 20 US states
item.description: Authors found wildfire-specific PM 2.5 showed greater toxicity per unit exposure than non-wildfire PM 2.5 for cardiopulmonary hospitalizations. As wildfire smoke becomes a major and growing source of air pollution, stronger mitigation strategies are needed.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic architecture of MRI-derived cervical spinal cord morphology reveals sensory-motor axis and systemic disease associations
item.description: A genome-wide association study of cervical spinal cord morphology using UK Biobank brain MRI data identifies 179 genetic loci shaping spinal cord morphology, revealing its links to systemic health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions
item.description: Here, the authors develop Autism-CLIP, a vision–language model for automated early autism screening using 3-min home videos of toddlers aged 15–24 months.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study
item.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is clinically heterogeneous, complicating efforts to identify patients at highest risk. Here, the authors show that integrating proteomics with machine learning reveals two biologically distinct subtypes with different prognoses, including a high-risk inflammatory cardiorenal phenotype.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sero-catalytic and spatial modeling of dengue virus force of infection in Timor-Leste
item.description: Dengue is a public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions. Here, the authors present findings from a national, population-representative serological survey in Timor Leste and identify substantial spatial variation in force of infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effectiveness of the oral rotavirus vaccine ROTASIIL among children hospitalized with acute gastroenteritis in India
item.description: Here, using pooled data from two multi-center observational studies, the authors analyze the effectiveness of the ROTASIIL ® vaccine in protecting young children against moderate to severe rotavirus diarrhea, finding that three doses of this vaccine provided good protection, especially among younger children, highlighting the need for timely and complete vaccination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Compound Z247611722 Exhibits Antifungal Activity by Inhibiting Serine Palmitoyltransferase
item.description: This study identifies and characterizes Z247611722, a novel fungicidal compound active against multiple Candida species, and demonstrates that it inhibits sphingolipid biosynthesis by targeting serine palmitoyltransferase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma autoantibody profiling via PhIP-seq and machine learning for diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is often diagnosed in later stages, which limits potential treatment options. Here, the authors develop a PhIP-seq model to diagnose oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma across multiple cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Next-generation functional diagnostic paradigm for musculoskeletal diseases based on live SWIR imaging
item.description: Here, the authors develop a live SWIR imaging strategy to enable dynamic, multi-component functional diagnosis of musculoskeletal diseases. It visualizes synovial fluid flow during locomotion, reveals patellar maltracking, and shows bone and vascular kinematics during healing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preclinical and clinical investigation of VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin receptor inhibitor for the treatment of frontotemporal dementia: a first-in-human randomized placebo-controlled phase 1 trial
item.description: Treatment for frontotemporal dementia due to GRN haploinsufficiency (FTD-GRN) are lacking. Here, in this preclinical and Phase 1 clinical trial, the authors show that VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin inhibitor, is safe and well tolerated, and increased progranulin levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early coconut oil exposure suppresses chronic experimental Crohn’s disease via myristic acid and enhanced regulatory T cells
item.description: Here, the authors show that coconut oil and the fatty acid myristic acid suppress Crohn disease-like intestinal inflammation in mice through multiple mechanisms, supporting a potential role for these dietary fats in promoting protective immune gut responses in Crohn’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: CpG hypermethylation and WNT/AP-1 cooperativity define the epigenetic landscape and a clinical subgroup of high-risk pediatric adrenocortical carcinoma
item.description: Pediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACTs) are rare and difficult to treat. Here, the authors perform integrated multi-omics analysis of 214 pACTs and identify four distinct risk groups and potential therapeutic targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Angiotensin II exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage in mice via heparin-like antithrombin activation and coagulation dysfunction
item.description: Here, the authors show that angiotensin II acts as a key coagulation regulator with heparin-like antithrombin activation function in mediating hemorrhage. Targeting the angiotensin II coagulation pathway could be a novel strategy to mitigate cerebral bleeding events.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global brain activity links subcortical degeneration to cortical tau progressively across Braak regions over early Alzheimer’s disease stages
item.description: This study finds that reduced infra-slow global brain activity may link degeneration of a key subcortical cholinergic region to progressive cortical tau accumulation in early Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Huntington’s disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation
item.description: Here the authors map Huntington’s pathology by barrier and vessel type with two-photon imaging, mass-spec signatures and mouse/human data. They reveal arteriolar susceptibility, spatially matched astrocyte activation and S1pr1 stimulation as potential therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: PKM2 AP: a micropeptide inhibits vascular calcification via molecular glue-mediated ubiquitination of PKM2
item.description: The study identifies a micropeptide that protects against vascular calcification, a major complication of chronic kidney disease. The micropeptide acts through a molecular glue-like mechanism to promote PKM2 degradation, suppress glycolysis and reduce vascular calcification in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic loneliness and isolation phenotypes and physical and mental health in older adults
item.description: Chronic loneliness was associated with poorer physical and mental health, while loneliness onset showed similar but weaker associations. Social isolation primarily affected mental health, while remission may confer cognitive benefits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Urban exposures, frailty, and mental illness in World Trade Center Health Program responders
item.description: Higher exposure to long-term air pollution, heat, and less neighborhood greenery is linked to increase in frailty and mental illness test scores among the World Trade Center (WTC) responders. These effects were stronger among those with higher WTC-related exposure histories.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of IgLON5 autoantibody recognition in autoimmune encephalitis
item.description: Anti-IgLON5 disease is a rare neuro-immunological disorder characterized by the production of autoantibodies against the cell adhesion molecule, IgLON5. Here, the authors examine the B cell receptor repertoire of an individual with this condition and present a cryo–electron microscopy structure of a patient-derived antibody clone in complex with IgLON5.

item.title: Nature Communications: LGR5-positive fibroblasts orchestrate skin mechanoadaptation through JAK1 modulation
item.description: Mechanical stress induces LGR5+ fibroblasts that promote adaptive tissue remodeling by limiting fibrosis through JAK1 modulation. The study reveals a conserved mechanism of adaptation to mechanical stress and suggests a strategy for regenerative therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo CRISPR screens identify dual functions of DNMT3A in mediating tumor immune evasion
item.description: DNMT3A regulates the anti-tumor activity of CAR-T cells. Here, based on in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors identify tumor cell-intrinsic DNMT3A as a mediator of immune evasion, showing that DNMT3A modulates TNF signalling and cholesterol biosynthesis to impair CD8 T cell anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiac fibroblast deletion of PTBP1 modulates the profibrotic response by alternative splicing
item.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of cardiac fibroblast phenotypes during fibrotic cardiac remodeling remains poorly defined. Here, the authors demonstrate that RNA-binding protein PTBP1 regulates alternative splicing to direct the profibrotic response in multiple cardiac injury models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proteasome inhibition alleviates proteinuria in Lmx1b knock-in mice with dysfunctional LIM domains
item.description: Mutations in the LIM domains of LMX1B cause ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and result in podocyte injury. Inhibition of the proteasome ameliorated renal symptoms in Lmx1b knock-in mice, thus providing proof of principle for a novel therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the consequences of childhood adiposity on the human plasma proteome at four timepoints across the lifecourse
item.description: Childhood obesity can influence health across the lifespan, but its molecular effects at different ages are not fully understood. Here, the authors use lifecourse genetics to show that childhood adiposity alters circulating proteins from childhood into adulthood, identifying potential links to childhood asthma and breast cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vascular and lymphatic dysregulation via non-EndoMT Col2a1 signaling in bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw
item.description: Bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) is a severe complication of antiresorptive therapy with poorly understood vascular mechanisms. Here, the authors identify vascular and lymphatic drivers of BRONJ and show that genetic ablation or silencing of Col2a1 restores endothelial homeostasis and rescues osteonecrotic lesions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Decoding the genomic repertoire of fosfomycin resistance genes in staphylococci
item.description: Here, the authors use 17,000 public genomes to systematically classify and unify nomenclature for fosfomycin resistance genes in Staphylococcus .

item.title: Nature Communications: Fecal microbiota transplantation for the decolonization of mucosal adherent-invasive Escherichia coli in Crohn’s disease: an open-label pilot study
item.description: Here, in a pilot study in humans, the authors provide proof of concept that fecal microbiota transplantation can be used for clearing harmful E. coli from the gut lining of people with Crohn’s disease, highlighting the potential of microbiome-targeted therapies in inflammatory bowel disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Assessing the use of automatic speech recognition and large language models for individuals with language impairments
item.description: Speech-enabled AI systems may be less reliable for people with language impairments. Here, the authors evaluate ASR-LLM pipelines across aphasia, child language impairment and dementia datasets, identifying transcript errors, repetition, and length as key factors affecting performance.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nested case-control study of air pollution and congenital heart defects via circulating proteins
item.description: Prenatal exposure to air pollution has been linked to risk of congenital heart defects (CHD). Here the authors report that periconception exposure, especially to NO₂, is associated with higher CHD risk and distinct maternal and cord blood protein signatures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atlas of genetic architecture and exploratory temporal interaction networks of plasma protein-based organ and system aging
item.description: This study provides a comprehensive atlas integrating genetic, environmental, and interactive insights into organ and system aging using multiple plasma protein-based networks, informing future research on targeted anti-aging strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: A dual-site oral nanovaccine programs anti-colorectal tumor immunity from small intestinal priming to large intestinal boosting
item.description: Here the authors report the design and characterization of a nano-vaccine composed of antigen- and CpG-loaded nanoparticles stabilized by β glucan and plant-derived lipids, showing that, after oral administration, it induces immune priming in the small intestine as well as acts as in situ vaccine to trigger anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer.
